content.title: About
content.content: Winter melon (also known as white gourd) becomes tender and mildly sweet after cooking. It is high in water, low in calories, and provides modest amounts of B‑vitamins, vitamin C, potassium and magnesium.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Winter melon is cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia, especially China, Thailand and India.
Raw fruits can weigh up to 50 kg, but they are usually cooked before consumption.
In traditional Chinese medicine the fruit is considered cooling and is used to help eliminate excess fluid.
In Japan cooked winter melon is used in sweet desserts such as mochi and jelly.
Its dense texture makes it a popular meat substitute in vegetarian and vegan dishes.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Cooked winter melon provides about 20 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potassium supports fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and is essential for collagen synthesis.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in the fruit promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Phytonutrients such as carotenoids help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions, including skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Winter melon contains low levels of oxalates, so people prone to kidney stones should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: When grown under poor conditions, pesticide residues may be present; choose organic or wash thoroughly before cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked winter melon can be diced and added to soups, stews, curries or salads. It is also used to make purees, casseroles and sweet desserts such as jelly or mousse.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked winter melon in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer keeping, freeze it in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months.
